chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
He who takes the lead in oppression has to bite his hand (in repentance) tomorrow.

key_terms.الْبَادِي: The prominent / The one who takes the lead

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for an oppressor on the Day of Judgment according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the psychological and spiritual consequence of overt oppression, where the 'biting of the hand' symbolizes deep remorse for the opportunities and peace lost due to tyranny. This imagery echoes the Quranic description of the regretful sinner, emphasizing that the oppressor's own actions become the source of their eternal anguish. The statement serves as a warning that visible dominance in injustice ultimately leads to visible humiliation and self-inflicted sorrow in the Hereafter.
